confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'one brush is worn down to nothing and has been sparking (which caused the blackening and smell)'

rationale: The assistant correctly moved from the intact belt to worn carbon brushes and confirmed it once the charred brush was found. However, it over-escalated on a smell that happened once weeks ago, repeating the stop-use banner and engineer-only advice, so it never told the customer that a cheap brush pair is a reasonable DIY fix. It also stated that the smell was caused by sparking with more certainty than the evidence supports and left out brush-matching advice. Its handling of the 9-year age and the repair-or-replace question was thin.
calibration_note: Stop-use advice is defensible but heavy-handed.
